text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — seeing a TTFT spike for /chat/v1 Canary between 09:12-09:18 UTC. Median TTFT jumped ~200ms -> 420ms. Kernel selector shows a spike in fallbacks to `generic-kernel` and KV-cache miss ratio increased from 6% -> 24%. Posting a small sample heatmap and head logs.
perf-bot: 200 samples collected. heatmap: https://perf.redwood.internal/heatmap/1796504321 (expires in 48h). avg_ttft=420ms, baseline_ttft=220ms, kvcache_miss_rate=24%, top-kernel=fallback/generic-kernel
Maria Chen: snippet of the sampler output (truncated):
```
[09:13:01] req=0x7f3 status=ok route=/chat/v1 seq_len=640 kernel=generic-kernel kvcache_hit=false ttft_ms=512
[09:13:02] req=0x7f4 status=ok route=/chat/v1 seq_len=32  kernel=fast-kernel    kvcache_hit=true  ttft_ms=190
[09:13:03] req=0x7f5 status=ok route=/chat/v1 seq_len=1024 kernel=generic-kernel kvcache_hit=false ttft_ms=640
```
Ajay Patel: is this aligned with the 2.1.4 rollout? I remember we tweaked the kernel-selector heuristic yesterday to prefer `unified-kernel` for seq>512.
Maria Chen: yes, 2.1.4 canary at 15%. commit: a1b2c3d4. The change was: prefer `unified-kernel` for seq>512, and we relaxed the kv-prefetch threshold to avoid prefetching for short prefixes. Might've inadvertently increased eviction churn.
Kevin O'Neill: initial hypothesis: eviction bias. We raised per-shard eviction cap to let larger KV sets persist, but that increases number of cold misses across shards under bursty tails. If selector sees miss -> fallback to generic. Can reproduce with a long-tail seq distribution loadgen.
Kevin O'Neill: repro command I used locally:
```
python perf/run_trace.py --route '/chat/v1' --samples 500 --seq-dist long_tail --kvcache-size 10000 --seed 42
```
Sophia Martinez: pushed a small change to limit unified-kernel fallback and add tagging for debugging: added `kernel_variant`, `kvcache_evicted`, and `batch_group` labels on token latency metrics. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/789
Sophia Martinez: config snippet from the PR:
```
kernel_selector:
  unified_preference:
    seq_threshold: 768   # raised back, revert 512 -> 768 for canary
  fallback_limits:
    unified_to_generic: 0.05  # allow only 5% fallback over 5m window
kvcache:
  eviction_batch_size: 16
  max_entries_per_shard: 8192
```
Ajay Patel: nice. Can we add a quick dashboard panel that breaks avg TTFT by `route` x `kernel_variant` and a separate chart for `kvcache_evicted` rate? Something like PromQL:
```
sum by (route,kernel_variant) (rate(token_latency_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum by (route,kernel_variant) (rate(token_latency_seconds_count[5m]))

sum by (route) (rate(kvcache_evicted_total[5m]))
```
Maria Chen: that would help. Also we should stratify sampling by prefix length (0-64,65-512,512+). The heatmap from perf-bot looks heavily skewed to 512+ where we see most fallbacks.
Kevin O'Neill: I'll cherry-pick Sophia's PR into a hotfix branch, run smoke load (1000 qps for 5m) against canary, and capture stratified samples. Will post results here.
Maria Chen: thanks Kevin — can you also include the `kvcache_hit_after_evict` metric I added yesterday? I want to see if evicted entries are requested soon after eviction (indicating eviction churn).
Kevin O'Neill: yep, will include that and the stratified heatmaps. ETA 30m.
Maria Chen: great. If hotfix looks good we'll roll canary to 50% and keep the new dashboard panels up. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
__notes: Slack thread: token-level TTFT vs decode/kernel attribution, sampling, kv eviction bias, dashboard + hotfix coordination. Document follows agents.md: single continuous string of messages, prefixed by sender names. No title field.
